messages.subject: R/qtl2 version 0.8
messages.body_plain:
[Oops that last post had an unfortunate error in the code.]

There's a new version of R/qtl2 <http://kbroman.org/qtl2> (0.8) with some major changes. We've merged the separate packages qtl2geno, qtl2scan, qtl2plot, and qtl2db into a single package, qtl2 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2>. The function names are all the same, just rolled into a single package.

The qtl2convert package (for converting objects among the R/qtl, DOQTL, and R/qtl2 formats) remains a separate package.

To remove the old packages: remove.packages(paste0("qtl2", c("geno", "scan", "plot", "db")))

To install the new R/qtl2 package: install.packages("qtl2", repos="https://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

The user guide <http://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/user_guide.html> and other documentation <http://kbroman.org/qtl2/docs> have been revised to reflect the changes.

karl

Best regards,
Guillaume.

messages.subject: Re: riself4 format
messages.body_plain:
It is possible to extend R/qtl2 to handle not-fully-fixed riself4-type crosses.

The key ingredients were actually derived in the Haldane and Waddington (1931) paper; see also my 2012 Genetics paper https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.111.132647

There is a bit of algebra to be done, but it's straightforward.

How many generations of inbreeding have you done for the different lines?

karl

Try table(geno) where geno is the object you're passing to plot_pxg(). Yes; as you say, perhaps one of the genotypes is not present at this locus.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Effect Plots for RQTL2
messages.body_plain:
>
> Ok, I think I need to take a step back... I don't think I understand what maxmarg() does.
>
> 1) Is the output of maxmarg() telling me what founder genotype each of my samples looks like at the given locus?

For each individual, it returns the genotype with highest probability, provided it is > minprob (which has a default value of 0.95).

> 2)  Is the fact that one of the founder strains isn't present on the plot_pxg() graph indicative that none of the samples look like this founder strain at the given locus?
>

Yes, I think so.

karl
